objective: Complete hosted Sandbox Fabric integration for OpenComputer and Blaxel with provider-native lifecycle, connection catalog, ComputePool registration, and live physical CAS/F07 qualification.

rulesConsidered: Hosted sandboxes remain separate from Notebook Fabric and API/GPU Fabric.
Sandbox connections do not grant F06 production-worker authority.
Provider completion is not artifact acceptance; CAS and F07 remain authoritative.
Raw provider secrets remain server-side and never enter telemetry, evidence, or MCP payloads.
Optional provider SDKs must not become mandatory for the baseline FactoryOS typecheck.

notes: Provider secrets were not added to source; live credentials are GitHub Actions secrets.

changes: Added OpenComputerSandboxAdapter using the official TypeScript SDK and API key authentication.
Added BlaxelSandboxAdapter using @blaxel/core and BL_API_KEY/BL_WORKSPACE authentication.
Extended the canonical sandbox and compute provider types.
Registered both providers in SandboxRegistry, SandboxConnectionService, ComputeConnectionCatalog, and ComputeGateway/ComputePool.
Generalized hosted sandbox credential and template handling.
Added contract boundary verification, provider tests, and live physical CAS/F07 proof coverage.
Updated sandbox activation and architecture documentation.
Extended the unified live-multi-provider render harness and connection-hub tests for OpenComputer and Blaxel.
Scoped Lightning physical-proof concurrency by branch so independent PRs no longer cancel each other.
externalVerification: OpenComputer current TypeScript SDK documents Sandbox.create/connect, exec.run, filesystem read/write, and kill.
Blaxel current TypeScript SDK documents SandboxInstance.createIfNotExists/get/delete, process.exec, filesystem operations, and BL_WORKSPACE/BL_API_KEY authentication.
verificationPlan: Pass Sandbox Fabric provider-boundary verification and contract tests.
Pass strict FactoryOS typecheck and compute-pool/connection-hub validation.
Run applicable repository security and governance gates.
Run Live Hosted Sandbox Render Proof with OPENCOMPUTER and BLAXEL repository secrets.
Require physical MP4, independent CAS integrity, F07 physical verification, and signed receipt before physical qualification.
notes: OpenComputer and Blaxel are implementation-complete but remain physically unqualified until their live provider-specific proof runs pass.
The integration does not promote either provider into production F06 authority.

Branch-scoped Lightning proof concurrency has been added; a fresh validation cohort is required for the updated PR head. OpenComputer and Blaxel remain outside production-worker eligibility until live F07 proof.

Blaxel physical qualification passed in GitHub Actions run 38510539669: evidence artifact 11868869906 records MP4 SHA-256 93a2e258eec975e848214c7f0ffec0bea1df86a1936b7f400ceba10ef7aae0d7, byte length 5201, matching CAS reference, F07 outcome READY, publishAllowed=true, and receiptSignatureVerified=true.

OpenComputer physical qualification was attempted twice in run 38510539669. Both attempts failed at Sandbox.create with HTTP 503: no cells available with capacity. Neither attempt produced the physical MP4/F07 evidence artifact; this is recorded as a provider-side capacity blocker, not as a successful qualification.

At the verification snapshot, sandbox-fabric, Compute Pool, connection-hub, Team Change Gate, and OKF Governance Gate passed on PR head 4ffea03ce94e0ef96e1d8ce84000d1af67613359. Repository CI and Lightning physical proof were still running.

The temporary physical-proof trigger has been removed; the branch workflow is restored to its original workflow_dispatch-only configuration. OpenComputer and Blaxel remain productionWorkerEligible=false.
dispositionRationale: Blaxel now has verified physical MP4 + CAS + signed F07 evidence. OpenComputer remains physically blocked after two upstream HTTP 503 capacity failures. Core dedicated integration/governance checks passed, but CI/Lightning proof and full Strix review were not complete at the reconciliation snapshot. Keep both providers outside F06 production-worker eligibility, and do not merge until the remaining release/security requirements and OpenComputer physical evidence are resolved.
